records.label: Fresh vegetables (except potatoes and pulse crops)

records.definition: This class comprises fresh vegetables, except potatoes and pulse crops. Vegetables are temporary crops cultivated principally for human consumption both as field crops and garden crops, in the open and under protective cover. Certain gramineous and leguminous plants, if harvested while green for their green grains or for their green pods (for example, green peas, string beans, green maize) are treated as fresh vegetables, but if harvested for their dry grains or seeds, are classified as cereals and pulse crops.

records.label: Coal
records.path: Coal
records.definition: This group comprises coal, a combustible black (hard coal) and brownish-black (brown coal) rock consisting of more than 50% by weight and more than 70% by volume of carbonaceous material. It is formed from plant remains that have been compacted, hardened and chemically altered, and metamorphosed by heat and pressure over geologic time.

records.label: Hard coal
records.path: Coal / Hard coal
records.definition: This class comprises black coal ranked as hard coal, which includes anthracite and bituminous coal. Hard coal refers to coal of gross calorific value equal to or greater than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis and with a mean random reflectance of vitrinite of at least 0.6%.

records.label: Anthracite
records.path: Coal / Hard coal / Anthracite
records.definition: This subclass comprises anthracite, a high rank hard, lustrous black coal destined primarily for residential and industrial (as steel making) or commercial applications. It has generally less than 10% volatile matter and a high carbon content (about 90% fixed carbon). Its gross calorific value is equal to or greater than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis.

records.label: Anthracite
records.path: Coal / Hard coal / Anthracite / Anthracite
records.definition: High rank hard lustrous black coal destined primarily for residential and industrial (as steel making) or commercial applications. It has generally less than 10% volatile matter and a high carbon content (about 90% fixed carbon). Its gross calorific value is equal to or greater than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis.

records.label: Bituminous coal
records.path: Coal / Hard coal / Bituminous coal
records.definition: This subclass comprises coking or metallurgical coal and other bituminous coal. Bituminous coal is a medium rank coal used for gasification, industrial coking and heat raising, and residential heat raising. It is characterized by higher volatile matter than anthracite (more than 10%) and lower carbon content (less than 90% fixed carbon). Its gross calorific value is equal to or greater than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis.

records.label: Coking (metallurgical) coal
records.path: Coal / Hard coal / Bituminous coal / Coking (metallurgical) coal
records.definition: Bituminous coal with a quality that allows the production of a coke suitable to support a blast furnace charge. Its gross calorific value is equal to or greater than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis.

records.label: Other bituminous coal
records.path: Coal / Hard coal / Bituminous coal / Other bituminous coal
records.definition: Other bituminous coal mainly used for steam raising purposes. It is characterized by higher volatile matter than anthracite (more than 10%) and lower carbon content (less than 90% fixed carbon). records.label: Cannabis products
records.path: Cannabis products
records.definition: This group comprises cannabis viable seeds and vegetative plants; fresh and dried cannabis (buds and leaves); cannabis oil; other cannabis extracts and concentrates; cannabis-infused edible products; and other cannabis products n.e.c., for non-medical (recreational, wellness, lifestyle, spiritual, etc.) and medical uses. A plant of the genus Cannabis refers generally to three varieties which are cannabis Sativa, cannabis Indica and cannabis Ruderalis. Sativas and Indicas are the most commonly used cannabis strains for cultivation and propagation. The genetics of the different cannabis strains are widely mixed or cloned to create cannabis hybrids. Cannabis contains a number of active elements, including cannabinoids such as tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) or dronabinol, cannabidiol (CBD) and terpenes (aromatic compounds or chemical markers). Cannabis plants containing 0.3% w/w (weight for weight) of THC or less in the flowering tops and leaves - industrial hemp - and their derivatives with the THC concentration of 10 µg/g or less, as well as prescription drugs or pharmaceuticals containing cannabis, are excluded from this group.

Cannabis seeds and vegetative plants are commonly from three varieties which are cannabis Sativa, cannabis Indica and cannabis Ruderalis. records.label: Prefabricated buildings and components thereof
records.path: Prefabricated buildings and components thereof
records.definition:
This group comprises prefabricated buildings that are built in a factory or manufacturing facility and delivered to the construction site, and the components of prefabricated buildings built in a factory to be assembled later at a construction site. Prefabricated (factory-built) buildings are virtually complete and either unassembled or fully assembled (or manufactured) and ready to use; they can also be incomplete buildings, whether or not assembled, having the essential character of factory-built or prefabricated buildings. Prefabricated buildings can be used for residential or non-residential purposes.

A building refers to any roofed independent free-standing permanent construction or structure usually enclosed within external walls or dividing walls that extend from the foundations to the roof and comprises one or more rooms or other space. A building can be entered or accessed by persons or animals and is suitable or intended for protecting them and objects. A building can also include a separately usable underground construction.

A residential building refers to a construction in which at least half of the overall useful floor area is used or intended for residential or dwelling purposes.

A non-residential building refers to a construction in which more than half of the overall useful floor area is used or intended for non-residential purposes.

Prefabricated (factory-built) metal and non-wood buildings are virtually complete and unassembled; they can also be incomplete buildings, whether or not assembled, having the essential character of factory-built or prefabricated buildings, and delivered to the construction site. Components of these buildings are built in a factory to be assembled later at a construction site. Prefabricated buildings can be used for residential or non-residential purposes.

records.label: Station-to-station transportation of small packages and documents without tracking
records.path: Postal and courier services / Courier, parcel, and local messenger and delivery services / Station-to-station transportation of small packages and documents without tracking
records.definition: This subclass comprises transportation of small packages and documents without tracking of each package and document. Service is typically station-to-station but may be door-to-door. Transportation is provided on passenger buses and trains according to published schedules but departure and arrival times are not guaranteed. May include collect on delivery (C.O.D.) service. May include declared value coverage.

records.label: Station-to-station transportation of small packages and documents without tracking

May include declared value coverage.

records.label: Courier and messenger services
records.path: Postal and courier services / Courier, parcel, and local messenger and delivery services / Courier and messenger services
records.definition: This subclass comprises transportation and delivery, by a definite day and possibly by a definite time, of small packages and documents, with tracking of each package and document. Delivery by the scheduled day or specified time may be guaranteed. Small packages usually can be handled by one person without using special equipment. Service is typically door-to-door, although there may be options for the shipper to drop a package off and for the receiver to pick it up, and occasional shippers may have to drop off their packages. Pick-up and delivery outside normal service area or outside normal service hours, and pick-up on demand or on a regular schedule, are covered here. Service may include customs clearance. May include collect on delivery (C.O.D.) service. May include declared value coverage.

records.label: Same-day courier and messenger services
records.path: Postal and courier services / Courier, parcel, and local messenger and delivery services / Courier and messenger services / Same-day courier and messenger services
records.definition: Transportation and delivery, on the same day as pick-up and possibly by a definite time, of small packages and documents, with tracking of each package and document. Delivery on the day or by the specified time may be guaranteed. Small packages usually can be handled by one person without using special equipment. Service is typically door-to-door, although there may be options for the shipper to drop a package off and for the receiver to pick it up, and occasional shippers may have to drop off their packages. Pick-up and delivery outside normal service area or outside normal service hours, and pick-up on demand or on a regular schedule, are covered here. Service may include customs clearance. May include collect on delivery (C.O.D.) service. May include declared value coverage.

records.label: Next-day courier and messenger services
records.path: Postal and courier services / Courier, parcel, and local messenger and delivery services / Courier and messenger services / Next-day courier and messenger services
records.definition: Transportation and delivery, on the first business day or first calendar day following pick-up, and possibly by a definite time, of small packages and documents, with tracking of each package and document. Delivery by the scheduled day or specified time may be guaranteed. Small packages usually can be handled by one person without using special equipment. Service is typically door-to-door, although there may be options for the shipper to drop a package off and for the receiver to pick it up, and occasional shippers may have to drop off their packages. Pick-up and delivery outside normal service area or outside normal service hours, and pick-up on demand or on a regular schedule, are covered here. Service may include customs clearance. Transportation may involve one or more types of vehicles, such as buses, subways, streetcars, commuter trains and ferries. Passengers are permitted to pay on a per-trip basis, and the fare may be calculated on a zone basis. Covers urban transit services whether paid for by passengers or by contracts.

In other cases, the fee charged is on the basis of the length of time for which the vehicle is reserved; there is normally a minimum length of time and/or a minimum tariff. The vehicle and driver are available to make a series of trips as directed by the customer during the period for which the vehicle has been reserved.

Passengers are not charged a per-trip fee. Covers school bus services whether paid for by passengers or by contracts.

Service is typically between a limited number of pick-up and drop-off points, with no local service for other points along the route; or on a circular route with frequent stops. The service is not part of a network. As many passengers as can be accommodated are carried on a first-come first-served basis. Passengers may or may not be charged a per-trip fee. Covers shuttle service whether paid for by passengers or by contracts.

Vehicles used are typically buses but may be smaller vehicles such as vans and cars, and may be accessible to people using wheelchairs and other mobility aids. Passengers are not charged a per-trip fee. Covers employee transportation to work whether paid for by passengers or by contracts. Carpool transportation is provided by arranging and administering pools and providing a vehicle to members of each pool in exchange for a monthly fee to cover operating costs. One or more pool members must act as driver.

Passengers are transported to and from their individual homes, workplaces and other locations. Passengers are charged a per-trip fee. Also comprises rental or operating leasing services of buses or coaches with operator or driver for a period of time, not generally dependent on distance. records.definition: Interurban transportation of passengers by rail, with premium-quality amenities, without sleeping facilities. The fare is not subject to advance purchase requirements or restrictions on exchanges or refunds. Covers the transport of accompanying luggage and other items as well as sales to passengers and bulk purchases by tour operators of seats for resale; exclusive and non-exclusive car usage; and scheduled and non-scheduled services. May include a segment where transportation is by bus. Covers service paid for with a ticket or voucher from a book of tickets, or with a train pass.

records.path: Passenger transportation services (including sightseeing) / Rail passenger transportation services / Rail passenger transportation services / Passenger rail transportation services, economy/discounted economy classes
records.definition: Interurban transportation of passengers by rail, with standard-quality amenities, without sleeping facilities. Food and beverages are available at an extra charge. Covers both economy and discounted economy classes; the latter offers the same amenities as the economy class but contains restrictions such as advance purchase and penalty charges for exchanges and refunds. Covers the transport of accompanying luggage and other items as well as sales to passengers and bulk purchases by tour operators of seats for resale; exclusive and non-exclusive car usage; and scheduled and non-scheduled services. May include a segment where transportation is by bus. Covers service paid for with a ticket or voucher from a book of tickets, or with a train pass.

records.definition: This class comprises coastal and Great Lakes fixed route passenger transportation services by water; and other passenger transportation services by water. Rental and leasing services of water passenger transportation vessels with operator or crew are included.

records.path: Passenger transportation services (including sightseeing) / Water passenger transportation services / Water passenger transportation services (except rental with operator)

records.definition: This subclass comprises rental or leasing services of all types of self-propelled passenger vessels for coastal, transoceanic and inland water transport, with operator or crew.

records.path: Passenger transportation services (including sightseeing) / Air passenger transportation services / Scheduled air passenger transportation services (except wet and damp leasing) / Scheduled air passenger transportation services, domestic
records.definition: Transportation of passengers by air on a domestic scheduled flight.

records.label: Scheduled air passenger transportation services, international
records.path: Passenger transportation services (including sightseeing) / Air passenger transportation services / Scheduled air passenger transportation services (except wet and damp leasing) / Scheduled air passenger transportation services, international
records.definition: Transportation of passengers by air on an international scheduled flight.

records.label: Air passenger charter transportation services
records.path: Passenger transportation services (including sightseeing) / Air passenger transportation services / Air passenger charter transportation services
records.definition: This subclass comprises rental and leasing of complete aircraft and crew, for the chartered or non-scheduled transportation of passengers and their accompanying baggage, equipment and supplies. Renters or lessees generally do not have operational control of the flights. Air charter services include air taxi, ad hoc air charter, frequent charter membership and full charter services. Full (public) air charter is a long-term renting of an entire aircraft, usually undertaken by tour operators, that require aircraft on a seasonal basis, but do not have the required infrastructure to operate their own aircraft.

records.label: Air passenger charter transportation services, domestic
records.path: Passenger transportation services (including sightseeing) / Air passenger transportation services / Air passenger charter transportation services / Air passenger charter transportation services, domestic
records.definition: Rental and leasing of complete aircraft and crew, for the non-scheduled transportation of passengers and their accompanying baggage, equipment and supplies, within Canada. Covers positioning fees, layover fees, and pilot standby fees. Renters or lessees generally do not have operational control of the flights.

records.label: Air passenger charter transportation services, international
records.path: Passenger transportation services (including sightseeing) / Air passenger transportation services / Air passenger charter transportation services / Air passenger charter transportation services, international
records.definition: Rental and leasing of complete aircraft and crew, for the non-scheduled transportation of passengers and their accompanying baggage, equipment and supplies, between Canada and other countries. Covers positioning fees, layover fees, and pilot standby fees. Renters or lessees generally do not have operational control of the flights.

records.label: Rental and leasing of passenger aircraft with operator or crew (except chartering)
records.path: Passenger transportation services (including sightseeing) / Air passenger transportation services / Rental and leasing of passenger aircraft with operator or crew (except chartering)
records.definition: This subclass comprises rental and leasing services of passenger aircraft or aircraft suitable for passenger and freight (including helicopters) with operator or crew (wet and damp leasing). A ''wet lease'' is a leasing arrangement whereby one "airline" or aircraft operator (the lessor) provides an aircraft, complete crew (''damp lease'' is with only cockpit crew), maintenance, and insurance (ACMI). These services are generally supplied on a time basis and several different destinations are frequently involved. The services may include providing fuel. Renters or lessees generally have operational control of the flights. The period of the rental or lease can go from one month to usually one to two years. Everything less than one month can be considered as ad-hoc charter services.

records.label: Rental and leasing of passenger aircraft with operator or crew (except chartering)

records.definition: Rental and leasing services of passenger aircraft or aircraft suitable for passenger and freight (including helicopters) with operator or crew (wet and damp leasing). A ''wet lease'' is a leasing arrangement whereby one "airline" or aircraft operator (the lessor) provides an aircraft, complete crew (''damp lease'' is with only cockpit crew), maintenance, and insurance (ACMI). These services are generally supplied on a time basis and several different destinations are frequently involved. The services may include providing fuel. Renters or lessees generally have operational control of the flights. The period of the rental or lease can go from one month to usually one to two years. Everything less than one month can be considered as ad-hoc charter services.

records.label: Scenic and sightseeing tour services

records.definition: This class comprises services which take customers to areas of scenic, historical or cultural interest by rail, buses and other ground vehicles, water, and air, and/or use vintage or specialized equipment that is an attraction in itself. records.label: Residential buildings
records.path: Residential buildings
records.definition:
This group comprises residential buildings.

A residential building refers to a construction in which at least half of the overall useful floor area is used or intended for residential or private dwelling purposes, whether on a permanent basis or not. Residential buildings normally provide accommodation units or residential building units with self-contained and exclusive use of bathroom and kitchen facilities to the occupants of each unit. At least half of the useful floor area must be used or intended for dwelling units, in the case of apartment buildings. A residential building unit is a structurally separated and independent place.
A group of three row houses that are attached is considered to be three separate buildings if their external walls or dividing walls extend from the foundations to the roof.

Residential buildings constructed entirely at the building site, as well as on-site fully assembled precast, panelized, modular and other prefabricated residential buildings are included in this group. Unassembled prefabricated residential buildings built in a factory, and manufactured or fully assembled residential buildings built in a factory and delivered ready for move-in, are excluded from this group.

A building for which the majority of the overall useful floor area is used or intended for dwelling units with shared bathroom and kitchen, or that area is used primarily to offer care and other assisted living services, is classified as a "collective dwelling-type building" under the non-residential buildings group.

A building refers to any independent free-standing permanent structure comprising one or more residential dwelling units, business units or other spaces. A building can be entered by persons or animals and is suitable or intended for protecting them and objects. A building is covered by a roof and is usually enclosed within external walls or dividing walls that extend from the foundations to the roof. In the case of interconnected structures (e.g., semi-detached or terraced houses), any unit separated from other units by a fire wall extending from roof to cellar is considered an individual building. If there is no fire wall, the interconnected building units are regarded as individual buildings if they have their own access (own entrance) as well as their own utility system and are separately usable.

Residential buildings constructed entirely at the building site, as well as on-site fully assembled precast, panelized, modular and other prefabricated residential buildings are included in this group. Unassembled prefabricated residential buildings built in a factory, and manufactured or fully assembled residential buildings built in a factory and delivered ready for move-in, are excluded from this group.

A building for which the majority of the overall useful floor area is used or intended for dwelling units with shared bathroom and kitchen, or that area is used primarily to offer care and other assisted living services, is classified as a "collective dwelling-type building" under the non-residential buildings group.

If there is no fire wall, the interconnected building units are regarded as individual buildings if they have their own access (own entrance) as well as their own utility system and are separately usable.

records.definition: This subclass comprises residential buildings of five or more storeys. A residential building of five or more storeys refers to such a building of which at least half of the overall useful floor area is used or intended for residential or dwelling purposes. A residential building also generally provides accommodation units with self-contained and exclusive use of bathroom and kitchen facilities to the occupants of the apartments, condominiums or other types of dwellings in the building. These types of buildings do not provide care or other assisted daily living services; they provide private dwellings for at least half of the overall useful floor area of the building.

Also a group of apartments, usually row-oriented, where each one is like a separate "house" and is usually two storeys. It generally refers to such units in an urban area and they are often condominiums. Often referred to as "townhouses".

records.label: Non-residential buildings
records.path: Non-residential buildings
records.definition:
This group comprises non-residential buildings.

A non-residential building refers to a construction in which more than half of the overall useful floor area is used or intended for non-residential purposes, namely for industrial, commercial or institutional purposes, including for the provision of services. A non-residential building unit is a structurally separated and independent place.

Non-residential buildings constructed entirely at the building site, as well as on-site fully assembled precast, panelized, modular and other prefabricated non-residential buildings are included in this group. Unassembled prefabricated non-residential buildings built in a factory, and manufactured or fully assembled non-residential buildings built in a factory and delivered ready for move-in, are excluded from this group.

A building for which more than half of the useful floor area is used or intended for dwelling units or accommodation units with shared bathroom and kitchen, or that area is used primarily to offer care and other assisted living services, is classified as a "collective dwelling-type building" in this group.

A building refers to any roofed independent free-standing permanent construction or structure usually enclosed within external walls or dividing walls that extend from the foundations to the roof and comprises one or more rooms or other space. A building can be entered or accessed by persons or animals and is suitable or intended for protecting them and objects. A building can also include a separately usable underground construction. In the case of interconnected structures, any unit separated from other units by a fire wall extending from roof to cellar is considered an individual building. If there is no fire wall, the interconnected building units are regarded as individual buildings if they have their own access or entrance, as well as their own utility system and are separately usable.

records.label: Research and experimental development services
records.path: Research and experimental development services
records.definition: This group comprises research and experimental development services in natural sciences, engineering and technology, medical and health sciences, agricultural and veterinary sciences, social sciences, and humanities and the arts. Research and experimental development (R&D) comprise creative and systemic work undertaken in order to increase the stock of knowledge - including knowledge of humankind, culture and society - and to devise new applications of available knowledge. The term R&D refers to three types of activity: basic research, applied research and experimental development. Basic research refers to experimental or theoretical work undertaken primarily to acquire new knowledge of the underlying foundations of phenomena and observable facts, without any particular application or use in view. Applied research refers to original investigation undertaken in order to acquire new knowledge. It is, however, directed primarily towards a specific, practical aim or objective. Experimental development is systematic work, drawing on knowledge gained from research and practical experience and producing additional knowledge, which is directed to producing new products or processes or to improving existing products or processes.

records.label: Sporting event media rights

records.definition: This subclass comprises the right to broadcast a sporting event on traditional electronic media and other media rights related to sporting events.

records.label: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services
records.definition: This group comprises fixed wholesale and retail telecommunications services; fixed wholesale and retail Internet access services; mobile wholesale and retail telecommunications services; cable, satellite, Internet and other fixed or mobile broadcasting distribution services of audiovisual and audio works; and online games, except gambling.

records.label: Wholesale telecommunications services (carrier services)
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Wholesale telecommunications services (carrier services)
records.definition: This class comprises fixed wholesale telecommunications and Internet access services, and mobile wholesale telecommunications.

records.label: Fixed wholesale telecommunications services (except Internet access)
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Wholesale telecommunications services (carrier services) / Fixed wholesale telecommunications services (except Internet access)
records.definition: This subclass comprises the provision of a fixed telecommunications service or facility by a telecommunications service provider to a provider of retail fixed telecommunications services. The purchaser may resell the service or facility to another entity, or use the service or facility to support the services it bills.

records.label: Fixed wholesale telecommunications services (except Internet access)
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Wholesale telecommunications services (carrier services) / Fixed wholesale telecommunications services (except Internet access) / Fixed wholesale telecommunications services (except Internet access)
records.definition: Provision of a fixed telecommunications service or facility by a telecommunications service provider to a provider of retail fixed telecommunications services. The purchaser may resell the service or facility to another entity, or use the service or facility to support the services it bills.

records.label: Fixed wholesale Internet access services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Wholesale telecommunications services (carrier services) / Fixed wholesale Internet access services
records.definition: This subclass comprises the provision of fixed Internet access and transport services by a telecommunications service provider to a provider of fixed retail Internet access services.

records.label: Fixed wholesale Internet access services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Wholesale telecommunications services (carrier services) / Fixed wholesale Internet access services / Fixed wholesale Internet access services
records.definition: Provision of fixed Internet access and transport services by a telecommunications service provider to a provider of fixed retail Internet access services.

records.label: Mobile wholesale telecommunications services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Wholesale telecommunications services (carrier services) / Mobile wholesale telecommunications services
records.definition: This subclass comprises the provision of a mobile telecommunications service or facility by a wireless telecommunications service provider to another to exchange traffic and extend service coverage area.

records.label: Mobile wholesale telecommunications services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Wholesale telecommunications services (carrier services) / Mobile wholesale telecommunications services / Mobile wholesale telecommunications services
records.definition: Provision of a mobile telecommunications service or facility by a wireless telecommunications service provider to another to exchange traffic and extend service coverage area.

records.label: Retail telecommunication services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Retail telecommunication services
records.definition: This class comprises fixed retail telecommunications and Internet access services, and mobile retail telecommunications.

records.label: Fixed retail telecommunications services (except Internet access)
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Retail telecommunication services / Fixed retail telecommunications services (except Internet access)
records.definition: This subclass comprises telephone services to end users where calls originate from a device connected to a landline.

records.label: Fixed local and access telecommunications services (except Internet access), at retail
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Retail telecommunication services / Fixed retail telecommunications services (except Internet access) / Fixed local and access telecommunications services (except Internet access), at retail
records.definition: A landline-based telephone service that allows end users to make calls within a defined local area and provides access to a long distance network of the customer's choice.

records.label: Fixed long distance telecommunications services (except Internet access), at retail
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Retail telecommunication services / Fixed retail telecommunications services (except Internet access) / Fixed long distance telecommunications services (except Internet access), at retail
records.definition: A landline-based telephone service allowing end users to make calls outside a local calling area.

records.label: Data transmission services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Retail telecommunication services / Fixed retail telecommunications services (except Internet access) / Data transmission services
records.definition: Telecommunications services making use of data protocols to transmit data over a public network.

records.label: Private network services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Retail telecommunication services / Fixed retail telecommunications services (except Internet access) / Private network services
records.definition: Telecommunications network segments for the exclusive use of the client on which no control or signalling is performed by the telecommunications service provider.

records.label: Fixed retail Internet access services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Retail telecommunication services / Fixed retail Internet access services
records.definition: This subclass comprises the provision of fixed connections (including fixed wireline and wireless) to the Internet to end users.

records.label: Dial-up Internet access services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Retail telecommunication services / Fixed retail Internet access services / Dial-up Internet access services
records.definition: Provision of fixed connections to the Internet to end users at download speeds not exceeding 64 Kbps. Dial-up Internet access is one of the oldest forms of Internet access technology. It is also referred to as low or narrowband speed Internet access. Narrowband is generally regarded as a category including any connection with a transmission or download speed of up to 1.5 Mbps.

records.label: Fixed high-speed Internet access services, residential
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Retail telecommunication services / Fixed retail Internet access services / Fixed high-speed Internet access services, residential
records.definition: Provision of fixed connections to the Internet to residential end users at download speeds generally greater than 256 Kbps. High-speed Internet is also referred to as broadband Internet, with fixed line types such as cable, digital subscriber line (DSL), terrestrial wireless access, direct-to-home satellite access, and fibre optic services. Even though the lowest speed limit for high-speed Internet is set to 256 Kbps in several countries, broadband is generally regarded as a category including any connection with a transmission or download speed of 1.5 Mbps or greater. Connection with download speed from 256 Kbps up to 1.5 Mbps is sometimes referred to as "wideband" or "lite broadband".

records.label: Fixed high-speed Internet access services, non-residential
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Retail telecommunication services / Fixed retail Internet access services / Fixed high-speed Internet access services, non-residential
records.definition: Provision of fixed connections to the Internet to non-residential or business end users at download speeds greater than 256 Kbps. High-speed Internet is also referred to as broadband Internet, with fixed line types such as cable, digital subscriber line (DSL), terrestrial wireless access, direct-to-home satellite access, and fibre optic services. Even though the lowest speed limit for high-speed Internet is set to 256 Kbps in several countries, broadband is generally regarded as a category including any connection with a transmission or download speed of 1.5 Mbps or greater. Connection with download speed from 256 Kbps up to 1.5 Mbps is sometimes referred to as "wideband" or "lite broadband".

records.label: Mobile retail telecommunications services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Retail telecommunication services / Mobile retail telecommunications services
records.definition: This subclass comprises telecommunication services to end users where voice or data communications originate from, or terminate into, a mobile device connected to a wireless network.

records.label: Mobile local and access telecommunications services, at retail
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Retail telecommunication services / Mobile retail telecommunications services / Mobile local and access telecommunications services, at retail
records.definition: A wireless-based telecommunications service that allows end users to make and receive calls within a defined local area and provides access to a long distance network of the customer's choice. Mobile cell phone plans typically bundle voice and text messaging.

records.label: Mobile long distance telecommunications services, at retail
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Retail telecommunication services / Mobile retail telecommunications services / Mobile long distance telecommunications services, at retail
records.definition: Wireless based telecommunications service allowing end users to make calls outside a local calling area.

records.label: Mobile data services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Retail telecommunication services / Mobile retail telecommunications services / Mobile data services
records.definition: A service plan providing end users mobile access to text and multimedia messaging, along with access to the Internet through the cellular network. This service is also referred as "wireless mobile Internet access", at retail.

records.label: Roaming services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Retail telecommunication services / Mobile retail telecommunications services / Roaming services
records.definition: A service that allows a cell phone subscriber to use his or her mobile device while in the service area of another service provider.

records.label: Broadcasting and online games distribution services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services
records.definition: This class comprises broadcast distribution services of audiovisual and audio works such as television programs, films, videos, sound recordings, via cable, satellite, Internet and other fixed and mobile distribution streams. Also covers distribution services for online games, except gambling, and installation services for connections to broadcasting distribution networks.

records.label: Basic television programming packages
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Basic television programming packages
records.definition: This subclass comprises basic television programming packages distribution services, via fixed or mobile devices.

records.label: Basic television programming packages (except online streaming)
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Basic television programming packages / Basic television programming packages (except online streaming)
records.definition: Providing a basic package of movie and television programming services, basically to a fixed device, except using online streaming, for a monthly subscription fee. Basic packages are any first level programming package that must be purchased before being able to purchase additional programming packages. The basic programming packages are delivered using traditional over-the-air (OTA), cable and satellite television.

records.label: Online streaming of basic programming packages
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Basic television programming packages / Online streaming of basic programming packages
records.definition: Providing a basic package of movie and television programming services over the Internet, to a fixed or mobile device, using online streaming, for a monthly subscription fee. Basic packages are any first level programming package that must be purchased before being able to purchase additional programming packages.

records.label: Discretionary television programming packages
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Discretionary television programming packages
records.definition: This subclass comprises discretionary television programming packages distribution services, via fixed or mobile devices.

records.label: Discretionary programming packages (except online streaming)
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Discretionary television programming packages / Discretionary programming packages (except online streaming)
records.definition: Providing movie and television programming services, in addition to those included in a basic package, for an additional monthly subscription fee, generally to a fixed device, except using online streaming. This programming service comprises bundles of channels or à la carte channels. The discretionary television programming packages are delivered using traditional cable and satellite television.

records.label: Online streaming of discretionary programming packages
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Discretionary television programming packages / Online streaming of discretionary programming packages
records.definition: Providing movie and television programming services over the Internet, in addition to those included in a basic package, for an additional monthly subscription fee, to a fixed or mobile device, using online streaming. This programming service comprises bundles of channels or à la carte channels.

records.label: Pay-per-view services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Pay-per-view services
records.definition: This subclass comprises pay-per-view services, via fixed or mobile devices. The broadcaster shows a pay-per-view program at the same broadcast time to everyone ordering it.

records.label: Pay-per-view services (except online streaming)
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Pay-per-view services / Pay-per-view services (except online streaming)
records.definition: Providing services which enable subscribers to television programming packages, to watch a specific program (movie or event) at the same broadcast time, generally at a fixed device, for an additional fee, except using online streaming. The pay-per-view services are delivered using traditional cable and satellite television.

records.label: Online streaming of pay-per-view programs
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Pay-per-view services / Online streaming of pay-per-view programs
records.definition: Providing services over the Internet which enable subscribers to television programming packages, to watch a specific program (movie or event) at the same broadcast time, on a fixed or mobile device, using online streaming, for an additional fee.

records.label: Television, movie and video on demand services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Television, movie and video on demand services
records.definition: This subclass comprises pay television, movie and other video on demand services (except pay-per-view), via fixed or mobile devices. Subscribers or viewers of video on demand are allowed to choose and watch broadcasts at any time, for a one time fee paid for each individual video that is on demand (transactional video on demand), or for a monthly or annual subscription fee (subscription video on demand) to have unlimited access to television programs, movies and any other types of videos during the time covered by the subscription.

records.label: Television, movie and video on demand (except online streaming)
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Television, movie and video on demand services / Television, movie and video on demand (except online streaming)
records.definition: Providing pay television, movie and other video on demand services (except per-pay-view), generally via fixed devices, except using online streaming. Subscribers or viewers to/of video on demand are allowed to choose and watch broadcasts at any time, usually for a one time fee paid for each individual video that is on demand (transactional video on demand). Video on demand services are delivered using traditional cable and satellite television.

records.label: Online on demand streaming of television, movie and video
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Television, movie and video on demand services / Online on demand streaming of television, movie and video
records.definition: Providing pay television, movie and other video on demand services (except pay-per-view) over the Internet, via fixed or mobile devices, using online streaming. Subscribers or viewers to/of video on demand are allowed to choose and watch broadcasts at any time, usually for a monthly or annual subscription fee (subscription video on demand) to have unlimited access to television programs, movies and any other types of videos during the time covered by the subscription.

records.label: Satellite radio and online audio streaming services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Satellite radio and online audio streaming services
records.definition: This subclass comprises pay satellite radio and online audio (such as music) streaming services.

records.label: Satellite radio services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Satellite radio and online audio streaming services / Satellite radio services
records.definition: Pay satellite radio services.

records.label: Online audio streaming services
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Satellite radio and online audio streaming services / Online audio streaming services
records.definition: Providing programming services (including self-programming), over the Internet, that comprise a single payment (fee) or a subscription, to a selection of radio shows, music and other audio recordings, streamed to fixed and mobile devices (Internet audio services). Subscribers are allowed to choose and stream contents at any time during the time covered by the payment or subscription.

records.label: Online gaming services (except gambling)
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Online gaming services (except gambling)
records.definition: This subclass comprises provision of various games to be played online, on a subscription or single payment (fee) basis, except gambling. The games are streamed over the Internet to fixed and mobile devices.

records.label: Online gaming services (except gambling)
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Online gaming services (except gambling) / Online gaming services (except gambling)
records.definition: Providing various games to be played online, on a subscription or single payment (fee) basis, except gambling. The games are streamed over the Internet to fixed and mobile devices.

records.label: Installation services for connections to broadcasting distribution networks
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Installation services for connections to broadcasting distribution networks
records.definition: This subclass comprises services of installing cables on the customer premises and/or installing outlets to connect to the program or broadcasting distribution networks.

records.label: Installation services for connections to broadcasting distribution networks
records.path: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services / Broadcasting and online games distribution services / Installation services for connections to broadcasting distribution networks / Installation services for connections to broadcasting distribution networks
records.definition: Providing installation of cables on the customer premises and/or installing outlets to connect to the program or broadcasting distribution networks.

records.label: Other information technology (IT) and information services
records.path: Other information technology (IT) and information services
records.definition: This group comprises data processing, hosting and related services, and other information technology (IT) and information services.

records.label: Data processing, hosting, and related services
records.path: Other information technology (IT) and information services / Data processing, hosting, and related services
records.definition: This class comprises services such as website hosting, application provisioning, business process management, infrastructure provisioning, network management, and information and document transformation.

records.label: Website hosting and domain name registration services
records.path: Other information technology (IT) and information services / Data processing, hosting, and related services / Website hosting and domain name registration services
records.definition: This subclass comprises the services of providing the infrastructure to host a customer's website and related files in a location that provides connection to the Internet or make their website accessible via the World Wide Web, and domain name registration services.

records.label: Website hosting services
records.path: Other information technology (IT) and information services / Data processing, hosting, and related services / Website hosting and domain name registration services / Website hosting services
records.definition: Services of providing the infrastructure to host a customer's website and related files in a location that provides connection to the Internet or make their website accessible via the World Wide Web.

records.label: Domain names registration services
records.path: Other information technology (IT) and information services / Data processing, hosting, and related services / Website hosting and domain name registration services / Domain names registration services
records.definition: Services of providing the registration of a domain name for a customer, by certified registrars and authorized resellers or affiliates.

records.label: Application service provisioning
records.path: Other information technology (IT) and information services / Data processing, hosting, and related services / Application service provisioning
records.definition: This subclass comprises the provision of leased software applications from a centralized, hosted, and managed computing environment (including cloud), customized to the needs of individual clients or for multi tenant access.

records.label: Application service provisioning (except software as a service, on cloud)
records.path: Other information technology (IT) and information services / Data processing, hosting, and related services / Application service provisioning / Application service provisioning (except software as a service, on cloud)
records.definition: Provision of leased software applications from a centralized, hosted, and managed computing environment, customized to the needs of each clients, except software as a service (SaaS), cloud-based or on demand.

records.label: Software as a service, on cloud
records.path: Other information technology (IT) and information services / Data processing, hosting, and related services / Application service provisioning / Software as a service, on cloud
records.definition: Provision of rented or leased software applications over the Internet, from a centralized, Internet-hosted, and managed cloud computing multi tenant environment, where all clients can use the same application, on demand, commonly (not exclusively) on a monthly or an annual fee basis. No installation of the application software is needed for the client.

records.label: Business process management services
records.path: Other information technology (IT) and information services / Data processing, hosting, and related services / Business process management services
records.definition: This subclass comprises a service that analyzes the way a business process is conducted, and identifies improvements that can be made by integrating existing and new software services, in order to improve information flows and increase automation of the process.

records.label: Business process management services
records.path: Other information technology (IT) and information services / Data processing, hosting, and related services / Business process management services / Business process management services
records.definition: Services that analyze the way a business process is conducted, and identifies improvements that can be made by integrating existing and new software services, in order to improve information flows and increase automation of the process.

records.label: Other information technology (IT) infrastructure provisioning services
records.path: Other information technology (IT) and information services / Data processing, hosting, and related services / Other information technology (IT) infrastructure provisioning services

records.label: Long-term staffing (payrolling) and co-employment services
records.path: Administrative and support services / Employment services / Long-term staffing (payrolling) and co-employment services
records.definition: This subclass comprises supplying personnel for extended work assignments. Under the terms of this arrangement, the client may recruit the person or persons hired by the staffing firm and assigned to the client's place of work, or transfer a portion of the client's existing workforce to the staffing firm. Long-term employees are placed on the payroll of the staffing firm, which is legally responsible for their actions, but when working they are supervised by the client. This service also covers a staffing arrangement in which an organization (i.e., a professional employer organization (PEO)) co-employs a client's workforce. The PEO and the client enter into a contractual agreement whereby the rights and responsibilities in respect of co-employees are shared or allocated, with the service provider assuming responsibility for certain activities as agreed with the client. The services range from basic to full-service packages.
